01 Antidepressants · class card

SNRIs

serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors · venlafaxine · desvenlafaxine · duloxetine

Practice
  1. 52-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder at a follow-up visit venlafaxine dose doubled 2 months ago; trazodone at bedtime no new drugs, salt or alcohol change BP 154/98 mm Hg, was 126/80 · HR 92/min → Venlafaxine → venlafaxine raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent way and is typically avoided in hypertension; trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and lowers blood pressure on standing
  2. 34-year-old woman stopped venlafaxine abruptly 2 days ago felt well for a year; ran out of pills now dizzy, nauseated, irritable, achy as if with flu T 37.0 °C · no seizures → Restart venlafaxine, then taper slowly → abrupt stops of venlafaxine, a short half-life drug, bring discontinuation symptoms within days, flu-like among them; restarting and tapering slowly treats them
  3. 29-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder has a pre-employment urine drug screen takes only venlafaxine; denies any drug use screen positive for phencyclidine calm, oriented · no nystagmus · BP 118/76 mm Hg → Venlafaxine cross-reactivity → venlafaxine can produce a false-positive phencyclidine result on a standard urine drug screen; she has none of the agitation or nystagmus of real use
